key_insight: A unified analytical model can diagnose where photoelectrochemical cells lose energy and translate those losses into design rules for improving performance.
engineering_relevance: The framework helps engineers compare BIJ and SEJ photoelectrodes, fit experimental I–V curves, and identify optimization targets such as better interfaces, co-catalysts, and nanostructuring.
method: Models ideal and real current-voltage behavior with physically meaningful parameters
Decomposes losses into thermodynamic, optical, recombination, and interfacial terms from fitted data
Uses efficiency maps and Sankey diagrams to visualize limits, bottlenecks, and energy flow
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation against literature results across solar water splitting, CO2 reduction, NH3 synthesis, and solar redox flow batteries, spanning both photovoltaic-grade and intermediate-bandgap materials.
watch_item: Because the framework relies on fitting experimental I-V data, its diagnostic accuracy depends on data quality and on whether the assumed loss parameters capture the real device physics.
paper_title: From Loss Diagnosis to Rational Design: A Unified Analytical Model for Photoelectrochemical Cells
